claims.text: During high-temperature sliding, overall wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu coating is governed by formation of a stable, coherent surface oxide layer.
During high-temperature sliding, microscopic deformation of the FeNiCrCoCu coating is governed by formation of a stable, coherent surface oxide layer.
The coherent oxide layer acts as a barrier to metal-to-metal contact.
Suppressing metal-to-metal contact reduces adhesive wear.
Adding 1 at.% Ti to the FeNiCrCoCu coating will produce the hypothesized changes relative to a Ti-free coating.
Adding 1 at.% Ti will reduce wear rate by 30% relative to the Ti-free baseline coating.
Adding 1 at.% Ti will reduce microscopic deformation by 25% relative to the Ti-free baseline coating.
The predictions are intended to hold at 700°C, a sliding speed of 0.1 m/s, and a normal load of 10 N.
Coating thickness, substrate material, and sliding conditions may influence wear resistance and deformation.
The hypothesis is falsified if both measured responses in the Ti-added coating fail to improve by at least 20% relative to the Ti-free coating.
